transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start time: 14:30 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alice Romero (Redwood AE), Ben Cho (Redwood SE), Marisol Vega (Ironclad - CISO), Jake Patel (Ironclad - Infra Eng), Darya Kline (Ironclad - Compliance)

00:00 Alice (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump into audit logs and admin activity, happy to take questions as we go.
00:12 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): Thanks, Alice. We mainly want to confirm what Redwood logs, how we can export them, and retention options for our SOC 2 and internal audits.
00:20 Ben (Redwood SE): Great. I'll run through the event model first, then exports, then retention and encryption. Note, I'm Ben, I'll call out a couple of things that sometimes get transcribed oddly in notes like K-V cache — that's the KV cache for model state.
00:35 Ben (Redwood SE): So at a high level we capture admin events and user-level events. Admin events: role changes, RBAC policy updates, SSO provisioning events (SCIM), API key creation/deletion, service principal actions, key rotations in K-M-S, model rollouts and canary changes, and config changes that affect routing or dedicated capacity.
00:50 Jake (Infra): When you say key rotations, does that include customer-managed KMS keys? We need to see the KMS key ids in the logs for our audit trails.
00:58 Ben (Redwood SE): Yes, we log the event indicating a key rotation happened and the key identifier (redacted if it's a full ARN), timestamp, actor, and request id. We don't include the raw key material obviously.
01:12 Darya (Compliance): For our auditors we need IP, user-agent, and the request id mapping back to requests. Do you capture those for admin console and API calls?
01:20 Ben (Redwood SE): Yes, standard fields per event are: actor (user/service), actor_id, timestamp, action_type, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, source_ip, user_agent, outcome (success/fail), and a truncated payload for context. Payloads are truncated by default and PII scrubbed unless you opt into raw request logging for a short window in a controlled pilot.
01:40 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): How about embeddings and prompt texts — those could contain PII. Can we avoid them in logs or mask them?
01:48 Alice (Redwood AE): We have log-sanitization settings. By default content is redacted from long-term audit logs; you can opt into richer short-term debug logs for a pilot where content is retained for X hours and then scrubbed. Ben can send the exact schema and fields.
02:02 Ben (Redwood SE): Right, by default we strip request bodies that look like user content for long-term retention. For compliance you can enable structured metadata for prompt length, token counts, model id, but not raw text unless you explicitly enable it for a defined retention window.
02:20 Jake (Infra): Export options — we want continuous streaming into our Splunk indexer. Does Redwood support syslog/Splunk forwarders?
02:28 Ben (Redwood SE): We support multiple export modes: batch export to S3 (JSONL), direct streaming to BigQuery for analytics, and syslog or HTTPS webhook streaming for SIEMs like Splunk or Datadog. For Splunk specifically we have a recommended connector pattern; we can either push via syslog or you can pull from S3 with a forwarder.
02:46 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): Retention: what is your default retention and what are paid options?
02:52 Alice (Redwood AE): Default is 90 days for audit logs in hosted. We offer a retention add-on for 1 year and multiyear archival (via cold storage) as a paid tier for enterprise customers. For Dedicated or Private deployments you can configure retention to meet your policy and keep logs in your own storage.
03:08 Darya (Compliance): If we choose Redwood-managed retention for longer than 90 days, is that stored encrypted with our KMS?
03:14 Ben (Redwood SE): Yes, logs at rest are encrypted. For hosted we encrypt with Redwood-managed keys by default; we offer customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own KMS) so the encryption keys are under your control. For the export to S3 we can deliver encrypted objects with SSE-KMS and you can supply the CMK.
03:30 Jake (Infra): Format details — is it one JSON event per line, and do you include a schema?
03:35 Ben (Redwood SE): Yes JSONL events, we include a stable schema and we will provide the JSON schema file. Each event is a single JSON line with the fields I mentioned earlier. Sample events and mapping for Splunk will be in the export doc.
03:50 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): What about administrative UI actions — console clicks, policy changes done through the GUI — are those included or only API actions?
03:58 Ben (Redwood SE): Both. The console is backed by the API so UI actions generate the same event types. We also capture who initiated the UI action and session metadata. Occasionally the transcription will show 'Speaker 1' for session but the event will have the user id.
04:16 Darya (Compliance): For audit purposes we need immutable logs for a period. Can Redwood guarantee immutability or append-only behavior?
04:24 Alice (Redwood AE): For hosted we provide an append-only store and tamper-evident controls; for ironclad-level immutability we recommend exporting to your S3 bucket with Object Lock in Governance mode or using your SIEM where you can enforce immutability policies.
04:42 Jake (Infra): How do you handle cross-region for data residency — we need EU-only storage for some logs.
04:48 Ben (Redwood SE): You can configure export targets by region. Redwood's hosted control plane can route logs to a region-specific export endpoint; for strict data residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment so logs never leave your VPC.
05:02 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): Anything about audit of admin activity for model rollouts and canaries? We need to be able to see who changed the model version and when, plus the previous version for rollback forensic.
05:12 Ben (Redwood SE): Yes, model rollout events are in the audit trail, include prev_version and new_version in the event metadata, actor, comment field if provided, and a request_id linking to deployment logs.
05:28 Darya (Compliance): Do you keep an export of admin console screenshots or just metadata?
05:34 Ben (Redwood SE): We do not store screenshots by default. We keep structured metadata. If you need richer records for an internal audit we can work on an integration to capture session transcripts, but typically that's not standard.
05:46 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): How about SSO and SCIM provisioning events for RBAC?
05:52 Ben (Redwood SE): We log SAML SSO events, SCIM provisioning events, role assignments, and failed SSO attempts. We can correlate SAML assertions to user ids in logs.
06:04 Jake (Infra): For incident response, can we get a live stream of events or is it only batch?
06:10 Ben (Redwood SE): Both. We support real-time webhook streaming to your incident system, with event-level delivery. We also support periodic batches to S3 for archival. Real-time streams are rate-limited, but designed for incident workflows.
06:24 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): Any red flags or limitations we should be aware of?
06:29 Ben (Redwood SE): A couple of caveats: if you enable raw request capture (prompts, responses) it's sensitive so we recommend strict retention and encryption. Also very high-volume sites may want Dedicated capacity for consistent event delivery SLA. Lastly, some field names in older schemas changed — we'll send a migration mapping.
06:45 Alice (Redwood AE): We're going to attach the SOC2 Type II, the schema, and examples in the follow-up email. Any other quick Qs before we wrap?
06:52 Jake (Infra): One small one — do you include request latency as an event attribute? It helps correlate slowdowns with admin actions.
06:58 Ben (Redwood SE): Yes latency_ms is included on API events.
07:04 Darya (Compliance): And for our auditors we need a sample report showing a sequence of events for role change -> key rotation -> API key revoke. Can you produce one?
07:12 Ben (Redwood SE): Yes, we can generate a redacted audit trail for that sequence. We'll include that in the export examples.
07:20 Marisol (Ironclad - CISO): Ok thanks — helpful. Let's recap next steps.
07:26 Alice (Redwood AE): Recap: I'll send SOC2 artifact and compliance checklist; Ben will send export schema, S3/Splunk integration notes, and retention options; Jake and Darya will confirm destination and required events list. We'll tentatively meet next week for pilot onboarding.
07:40 Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-typing of KMS/K-M-S and K-V cache appears as K-V cache; speaker labels may be simplified in auto transcript.
